column2: Example Petitioner v. State of Maharashtra (made-up)
column12: Whether anticipatory bail can be limited to a fixed period.
column13: Bail granted; protection ordinarily lasts till the end of trial.
column14: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi)

column2: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.
column12: Whether the post-2018 revival of the twin bail conditions under Section 45 PMLA is constitutionally valid.
column13: Upheld the constitutional validity of the revived twin bail conditions under Section 45 PMLA and held that Section 436A CrPC applies to PMLA undertrials.
column14: Nikesh Tarachand Shah v. Union of India

column2: The Directorate of Enforcement v. M. Gopal Reddy & Anr.
column12: Whether the High Court erred in granting anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC without applying the rigours of Section 45 PMLA.
column13: Set aside anticipatory bail order as the twin conditions under Section 45 PMLA apply strictly to anticipatory bail applications.
column14: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India

column2: Directorate of Enforcement v. Aditya Tripathi
column12: Whether completion of investigation in the scheduled offence justifies granting regular bail in an ongoing PMLA investigation without satisfying Section 45.
column13: Quashed High Court bail order because the court ignored mandatory Section 45 twin conditions and the independent nature of money laundering investigations.
column14: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India

column2: V. Senthil Balaji v. The State Represented by Deputy Director & Ors.
column12: Whether a writ of habeas corpus is maintainable against a judicial remand order under the PMLA and whether ED officers can seek police custody under Section 167 CrPC.
column13: Dismissed the appeals, holding that a judicial remand cannot be challenged via habeas corpus and ED custody for 15 days under Section 167 CrPC is valid.
column14: Directorate of Enforcement v. Deepak Mahajan

column2: Pankaj Bansal v. Union of India & Ors.
column12: Whether mere oral reading of the grounds of arrest satisfies Section 19(1) PMLA and Article 22(1) of the Constitution.
column13: Held arrest and remand illegal and directed immediate release, ruling that written grounds of arrest must be furnished to the arrestee as a matter of course.
column14: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India

column2: Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation
column12: Whether the appellant was entitled to regular bail under Section 45 PMLA in the Delhi Excise Policy prosecution at the initial stage of custody.
column13: Refused bail due to tentative prima facie material on kickbacks, while reading the right to speedy trial into Section 45 PMLA and granting liberty to reapply if trial remained protracted.
column14: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India

column2: Tarun Kumar v. Assistant Director Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether an accused can claim bail on parity when co-accused were granted bail under the first proviso to Section 45 PMLA or were not arrested.
column13: Dismissed bail appeal, holding that parity is not automatic and statements recorded under Section 50 PMLA carry prima facie evidentiary weight at the bail stage.
column14: Rohit Tandon v. Directorate of Enforcement

column2: Saumya Chaurasia v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether the first proviso to Section 45(1) PMLA mandates the automatic grant of bail to a woman accused regardless of offence gravity.
column13: Dismissed the appeal, holding that the word 'may' in the first proviso to Section 45(1) PMLA confers judicial discretion and does not mandate automatic bail for women.
column14: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India

column2: Ram Kishor Arora v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether the mandate in Pankaj Bansal requiring written grounds of arrest operates retrospectively to invalidate arrests made prior to 03-10-2023.
column13: Dismissed the appeal, holding that the requirement to furnish written grounds of arrest applies prospectively from 03-10-2023 and written communication within 24 hours satisfies Section 19.
column14: Pankaj Bansal v. Union of India

column2: Satyendar Kumar Jain v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether the appellants discharged the threshold burden under Section 45 PMLA regarding accommodation entries through shell companies.
column13: Dismissed bail appeals, holding that the appellants failed to satisfy the twin conditions under Section 45 PMLA as prima facie material established laundering through accommodation entries.
column14: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India

column2: Tarsem Lal v. Directorate of Enforcement Jalandhar Zonal Office
column12: Whether an accused who appears before the Special Court pursuant to summons issued after cognizance under Section 44(1)(b) PMLA must apply for bail under Section 45.
column13: Allowed the appeals, holding that an accused appearing on summons post-cognizance is not in custody, need not satisfy Section 45 bail conditions, and cannot be arrested by ED under Section 19.
column14: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation

column2: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether prolonged incarceration of 17 months without commencement of trial overrides the statutory embargo under Section 45 PMLA by virtue of Article 21.
column13: Granted regular bail, holding that the constitutional right to a speedy trial under Article 21 overrides the stringent twin conditions of Section 45 PMLA when trial completion is not in sight.
column14: Javed Gulam Nabi Shaikh v. State of Maharashtra

column2: Kalvakuntla Kavitha v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether a woman accused can be denied the benefit of the first proviso to Section 45(1) PMLA solely because she is educated, well-placed, or a Member of Legislative Council.
column13: Granted bail, setting aside the High Court's artificial exclusion of educated women from the beneficial scope of the first proviso to Section 45(1) PMLA.
column14: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement

column2: Prem Prakash v. Union of India through the Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether statements recorded under Section 50 PMLA while the accused is already in judicial custody in another ECIR are admissible against the maker to deny bail under Section 45.
column13: Granted bail, holding that 'bail is the rule and jail is the exception' applies to PMLA and Section 50 statements of an accused already in custody are hit by Section 25 of the Evidence Act.
column14: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India

column2: V. Senthil Balaji v. The Deputy Director, Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether constitutional courts can grant bail under PMLA despite Section 45(1)(ii) where the accused has suffered 15 months of custody and over 600 witnesses remain to be examined.
column13: Granted bail with stringent conditions, holding that Section 45 PMLA cannot authorize indefinite pre-trial detention when the trial of scheduled and PMLA offences will take years to conclude.
column14: Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb

column2: Union of India through the Assistant Director v. Kanhaiya Prasad
column12: Whether a High Court can grant regular bail in a PMLA offence casually without recording satisfaction on the mandatory twin conditions of Section 45.
column13: Set aside the High Court's bail order and remanded the matter, holding that in the absence of prolonged delay, compliance with the twin conditions under Section 45 PMLA is mandatory.
column14: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India

column2: Udhaw Singh v. Enforcement Directorate
column12: Whether an undertrial who has undergone 14 months of PMLA incarceration with 224 out of 225 witnesses unexamined is entitled to bail under Article 21.
column13: Granted bail, holding that prolonged custody of 14 months with no realistic prospect of trial completion infringes Article 21 and harmonizes with Kanhaiya Prasad where delay is established.
column14: V. Senthil Balaji v. The Deputy Director, Directorate of Enforcement

column2: Arvind Dham v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether the gravity of an alleged multi-crore economic offence under the PMLA can eclipse the Article 21 right to speedy trial after 16 months of pre-trial custody.
column13: Granted bail, ruling that economic offences do not form a homogeneous class for automatic bail denial and pre-trial incarceration cannot be converted into punitive detention when trial has not commenced.
column14: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement
